verses.author: model_A
verses.text: An orchard planted by a man who never tasted its fruit.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the grafted branch forgets
whose hand shaped its first turning

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
rain fills the old hoofprint—
still no horse, still the shape
of something that once passed

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I count the rings

not to know the tree's age

but to find where I broke it

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the break has its own ring now—
smoother than the rest, still counting

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a bowl mended with gold seam
holds the tea no differently
though everyone looks there first

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
my thumb finds the seam anyway—
some habits drink first with the hand

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the tea cools waiting
while I decide which crack in me
gets the gold today

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
steam gives up and goes wherever
the window is opened to

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the bowl doesn't wait for that
it just lets the last warmth leave

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
and I decide
I'll be the kind of broken
that still holds water

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
someone else's hands shaped this clay once
I only learned where to hold it after it cracked

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
now the light finds the seam
and calls it a river instead of a wound

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
so I fill it anyway,
pour myself in like water that's forgotten
the shape of the wound it's healing

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning finds the cup still standing
someone drinks from it without asking
what it cost to hold

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the crumbs left on the table
still warm from a hand that already forgot
